relations: Absolute pump-effort/error threshold constants do not transfer between plants: a supervisor tuned on a different tank system (different units, actuator range, and settling time) performed worse than no supervision at all when transplanted here unmodified (349 false positives, IAE 163 vs 95 for PID-only) because its thresholds were calibrated for that plant's scale, not this one's. Thresholds must be derived relative to this plant's own observed statistics (e.g. a ratio of recent-to-baseline effort within the telemetry window, or relative to nominal_target), not copied as fixed numbers.

This plant's default configuration (gamma_1=gamma_2=0.2) is in the non-minimum-phase regime, where most pump flow is routed through the delayed cross-coupling path rather than directly to its own tank. This causes real, sustained effort/error oscillation from control-loop interaction even with zero fault present - a naive 'any elevated effort is anomalous' rule will false-positive constantly on this normal background oscillation.

Comparing the first half of a telemetry window against its second half can only detect faults that ONSET inside the window: if the fault is already active when the window begins, the baseline half is contaminated and the diagnostic ratio stays near 1.0, so a persistent fault is systematically invisible no matter how large the threshold is set; a reference external to the window (nominal target or a sibling branch) is required.

In a plant with two symmetric branches, the ratio of effort-per-unit-sqrt(head) between the branches is itself a fault localizer: the healthy twin acts as a live reference, so a single-branch fault (leak) is detected even when it never clears and both branches are faulted from the start lose that asymmetry and need a second, per-tank signal.

A leak raises the effort needed to hold a head, so the effort/head ratio rises on the leaking branch; the cross-coupled twin often shows the OPPOSITE sign (extra cross-flow raises its level so its own pump backs off), meaning a detector that only flags ELEVATED effort/error naturally avoids false-positiving the coupled-but-healthy tank.

The signed-to-absolute error ratio (|mean error| / mean|error|) is a scale-free persistence indicator: a healthy non-minimum-phase loop oscillates around its setpoint (ratio low) while a fault that the loop cannot fully reject drives a one-sided error bias, so this ratio separates real faults from normal background oscillation without any absolute, plant-specific constant.

Normalising the cross-branch specific-effort ratio (pump effort per unit sqrt(head)) by its own early-window value cancels the plant's constant structural asymmetry (per-branch setpoint and hydraulic gain differences), so a twin-comparison detector stays silent in the healthy episode while still amplifying a single-branch fault whose onset lies inside the window.

A single scale-free error signal (level deficit relative to the nominal target, or signed-to-absolute error bias) is not sufficient on a non-minimum-phase plant: normal cross-coupled oscillation can push either one across threshold on its own, so anomaly flags must be the CONJUNCTION of an independent effort-based signal and an error-based signal, which keeps false positives at zero in never-faulted episodes.

When the supervisory setpoint reference and the diagnostic reference are the same nominal target, any setpoint reduction the supervisor itself makes is re-observed as a level deficit and can re-trigger the detector, creating a self-sustaining lower/restore loop; the reduction therefore has to be bounded well below the deficit threshold (here <= 2.5 cm, i.e. below ~8% of nominal).

For a leak on this plant the compensating effort rise is only ~1.2-1.4x because the non-minimum-phase coupling routes most flow through the delayed cross path, so any effort-ratio gate above ~1.3 is already blind to the fault regardless of how long the window is.

On this plant the closed loop fully absorbs a small leak in the tracking-error channel (episode IAE is bit-identical with and without any fault, 94.698 everywhere), so any detector whose primary evidence is error magnitude or error bias is structurally blind to it; the only persistent fault signature is the pump-effort-versus-head imbalance.

Because a leak raises the required effort and (if the loop saturates) lowers the head, the specific-effort ratio v/sqrt(h) has both effects pushing the SAME way, so the twin-branch asymmetry is amplified and never self-cancels - unlike a residual formed from the mass balance, whose sign flips depending on whether the controller compensates with effort or lets the level sag.

The healthy cross-branch specific-effort ratio is fixed by plant geometry and the nominal operating point (for gamma=0.2 it equals (0.8*u2/u1-0.2)/(0.8*u1/u2-0.2) with u_i=sqrt(h_i)), so a model-implied nominal offset sym0 lets a twin-comparison detector work even when the two tank setpoints are different, whereas assuming sym0=0 would false-positive under unequal setpoints.

Requiring the whole-window and the recent-half statistics to give the same directional verdict separately rejects random oscillation-driven false positives (limit-cycle swings average out over a full period but not consistently across two nested windows) while still firing on a genuinely persistent fault, giving persistence filtering without needing any absolute threshold.

In the cross-dominant four-tank (gamma=0.2) a leak on tank 1 is compensated mainly by pump 2, which feeds tank 1 through tank 3 with weight (1-gamma)=0.8, while pump 1 (direct weight 0.2) actually backs off: solving the steady-state balances gives v2-v1 = q1/((1-2*gamma)*k), so the specific-effort ratio (v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2)) FALLS for a tank-1 leak and RISES for a tank-2 leak - the opposite sign to the naive 'the leaking branch's own effort rises' heuristic, so a twin-ratio detector must map a LOW ratio to tank 1.

Because the leak is fully rejected by the loop (levels track, episode IAE is fault-invariant), the only observable is the pump-effort-versus-head imbalance; comparing the twin branches' specific effort v/sqrt(h) against the plant-geometry reference works with faults present from the very first sample, whereas any baseline drawn from the window itself stays contaminated and blind.

A twin-branch specific-effort ratio is structurally blind to a symmetric double leak (equal faults on both branches) because the ratio stays exactly at its healthy value; reducing missed detections in both_leaks requires a separate absolute (model-gain) reference, not a sharper ratio threshold.

A gate whose threshold lies outside the physical dynamic range of its own statistic is not a conservative detector but a silent no-op: an ELEVATED_RATIO gate of 1.8 applied to a plant whose fault-driven effort change is only ~1.2-1.4x never fires on ANY scenario, so the supervisor still returns a per-tank diagnosis while its whole score collapses to IAE + 300 x (fault-active steps). The first check on any detector should be that its statistic actually crosses its threshold on at least one faulty scenario.

In this scoring budget a step of detection latency on a genuine fault costs 300, a step of false positive on a tank that never faults costs 800, and a false positive in the never-faulted baseline episode is fatal (promotion tolerance ~0); the detector must therefore be tuned to guarantee literally zero flags on the never-faulted branch and only then made as fast as possible - a threshold chosen to balance FP and FN rates is systematically suboptimal here.

Because the outer loop nulls the level error completely (episode IAE is bit-identical with and without any fault, 94.698), the missed-anomaly count of a supervisor is a pure measure of detector silence/latency, not of threshold accuracy - so miss counts can be used directly as a latency budget when tuning a detector on this plant, and any detector whose primary evidence is error magnitude or error bias has exactly the same score as no detector at all.

With a silent detector the per-scenario score is just 94.698 + 300 x fault-active-steps, so the milder but longer episodes (250-step leaks) score WORSE than the more severe but shorter ones (199 steps): scenario ranking under a blind supervisor reflects fault DURATION, not fault severity, so tuning against the visible ranking can mislead.

The tracking-error channel of this plant is completely fault-invariant (episode IAE is bit-identical at 94.698 across every scenario, faulted or not), so a supervisory setpoint change cannot improve the IAE term at all - the setpoint channel is score-neutral and only the detection-latency term and the false-positive term move the score; the optimum is a pure detector plus a restoration policy that never leaves a residual gap.

Because the twin specific-effort reference is evaluated from the measured heads (u=sqrt(h)) rather than the commanded setpoints, a supervisor that lowers the flagged branch's demand enlarges that branch's relative leak and pushes the diagnostic deviation further from 1.0, so a bounded demand reduction cannot mask its own fault trigger or re-trigger the detector - the self-sustaining lower/restore loop only appears when the diagnostic and the setpoint reference are the same signal.

A zero false-positive result on the never-faulted baseline is not evidence that a detector works: a supervisor whose gates are individually unreachable (here an effort-ratio gate of 1.8 against a plant whose fault-driven effort change is ~1.2-1.4x, AND-ed with an error gate of 0.03 against a loop whose error channel is bit-identically fault-invariant) is identically silent, and silence scores exactly like a perfectly tuned detector on the baseline. Only the faulted scenarios' missed-anomaly counts separate a working detector from a no-op, so a conjunction of two signals must have each term checked for individual reachability on faulty data before it is trusted as a persistence filter.

The 'separate absolute model-gain reference' proposed for a symmetric double leak cannot actually be built from the telemetry window: at steady state there are two measured mass-balance equations and three unknowns (common plant gain, q1, q2), so an equal leak on both branches leaves no signature at all - it is unobservable unless the fault onset (a transient) lies inside the window. A candidate whose only diagnostic is a twin ratio therefore has a hard score floor of roughly (94.7 + 300*400)/6 ~ 2.0e4 on this battery, because the 120094-point both_leaks scenario survives untouched.

False-positive cost is not uniform within one episode: on any branch whose own fault never activates a flag costs 800, while on a branch that is itself faulted it costs only 160, so the correct design bias is a statistic that is automatically anti-correlated with the healthy twin's demand rather than a symmetric magnitude threshold. The cross-branch effort/head ratio has this property for free - the leaking branch's own pump throttles back while its cross-coupled partner takes the load - so the twin-ratio detector's residual FP risk lives almost entirely in the never-faulted baseline and in the settling window right after a fault clears, not in faulted episodes.
